editorial_thesis: The useful frontier is becoming operational: persistent identity, local inference capacity, and agent-readable web surfaces turn capable models into systems that can migrate, scale, and be used.

topic_groups.title: Persistent Agent State
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Coverage gap: the last dossier covered runtime placement, but not the durable identity, memory, code, and authority that make migration safe.

sources.title: Runtime-Independent Persistent Agents
sources.why_selected: Defines a migration protocol for identity, memory, code lineage, and continuation authority.
sources.usefulness: Provides a concrete checklist for durable agent state in Buildn workflows.

sources.title: Building a Memory-Driven Agent with NVIDIA NemoClaw
sources.why_selected: Separates evidence, human-readable knowledge, operational judgment, and governed execution.
sources.usefulness: Useful pattern for auditable client context and correction handling.

sources.title: NVIDIA OpenShell
sources.why_selected: Provides the sandbox/runtime governance layer referenced by the memory-driven agent pattern.
sources.usefulness: Candidate boundary for experiments that should not inherit host credentials.

sources.title: AgentScope Runtime
sources.why_selected: Fresh runtime infrastructure signal for deploying and operating agent applications.
sources.usefulness: Worth comparing with Hermes runtime abstractions before adding another control plane.

topic_groups.title: Local Inference + Edge Capacity
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Under-covered practical lane: local hardware can now be treated as a dynamic pool for parallel agent work instead of a single workstation endpoint.

sources.title: NVIDIA PAIR Virtual Inference Router
sources.why_selected: Routes independent Ollama/LM Studio jobs across changing local machines without harness changes.
sources.usefulness: A low-friction way to test private multi-agent throughput.

sources.title: Personal AI Router repository
sources.why_selected: Makes the local routing idea inspectable and trialable rather than a hosted promise.
sources.usefulness: Supports a bounded benchmark using existing local models.

sources.title: Building a memory-driven agent with NemoClaw
sources.why_selected: Connects local/runtime governance to a useful, stateful agent workload.
sources.usefulness: Suggests a realistic benchmark beyond raw tokens-per-second.

sources.title: NVIDIA AI agents hub
sources.why_selected: Current hub surfaces PAIR and NemoClaw as adjacent local-agent building blocks.
sources.usefulness: Good launchpad for checking compatibility and available reference implementations.

topic_groups.title: Agent-Ready Web + Sandboxing
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Coverage gap: moves from agent runtime internals to the public interface and execution surface—how sites expose machine-readable capability while generated code remains bounded.

sources.title: Agent Readiness Score
sources.why_selected: Offers a practical audit across discoverability, content, access control, and protocol discovery.
sources.usefulness: Immediate checklist for making Buildn and client sites easier for agents to use.

sources.title: Sandboxing AI Agents, 100× Faster
sources.why_selected: Shows isolate-per-request execution for generated code with explicit capabilities and egress control.
sources.usefulness: Relevant architecture for safe code-mode experiments.

sources.title: Markdown for Agents
sources.why_selected: Concrete content-negotiation pattern for machine-readable web delivery.
sources.usefulness: A small implementation that can improve retrieval quality immediately.

sources.title: Agent Access Model
sources.why_selected: Frames agents as software principals requiring identity, authorization, and accountability.
sources.usefulness: Keeps agent-readiness work from becoming an access-control afterthought.
